title: Composition coherence of exceptional internal-Hom exchange
statement:
Fix the coefficient conventions of [def-trf-coefficient-conventions], $A=A_{E,n}$. Let $C\xrightarrow{c}Z$ and $W\xrightarrow{j}C$ be composable separated finite-type morphisms of finite-type $k$-schemes, each exceptionally admissible at $A$ in the sense of [def-trf-admissibility], and let $M,N\in D^b_{ctf}(Z,A)$. For every admissible map $h$ write $E_h$ for the canonical exchange of [lem-trf-exceptional-internal-hom-exchange], with its ordinary pullback in the first variable and exceptional pullback in the second. Let $\kappa_Q:R(cj)^!Q\xrightarrow{\sim}Rj^!Rc^!Q$ be the specified composition comparison, for $Q=R\mathcal Hom_A(M,N)$. Under the canonical pullback and exceptional composition identifications, the exchange for the composite is coherent with the two exchanges: 
$$\kappa_Q\circ E_{cj}=Rj^!(E_c)\circ E_j.$$
Here the source of $E_j$ is identified with $R\mathcal Hom_A(Lj^*Lc^*M,Rj^!Rc^!N)$ and the source of $E_{cj}$ with $R\mathcal Hom_A(L(cj)^*M,R(cj)^!N)$; the displayed equality is an equality of the specified canonical maps after these identifications.

source.place: §0.3(a), equation (0.3), composition coherence of the exchange comparison

proof.text: Write $\mathcal D_T=D^b_{ctf}(T,A)$ and $H_T=R\mathcal Hom_A$. Put $F=Rc_!$, $G=Rc^!$, $L=Lc^*$ and $f=Rj_!$, $g=Rj^!$, $l=Lj^*$. The admissibility datum supplies $F\dashv G$, $f\dashv g$ and their constructible domains. The pullback-preservation lemma gives $LM\in\mathcal D_C$ and $lLM\in\mathcal D_W$. Set $Q=H_Z(M,N)$, $H=H_C(LM,GN)$ and $P=H_W(lLM,gGN)$; all three belong to their $\mathcal D_T$ by internal-Hom preservation and admissibility. Tensor preservation ensures that every tensor used below also lies in the relevant constructible domain. Use compact-support composition $Ff\cong R(cj)_!$ and pullback composition $L(cj)^*\cong lL$. By the specified exceptional comparison in admissibility, its conjugate identifies $R(cj)^!$ with $gG$, with the composite adjunction. Thus the composite has the required constructible adjunction and preservation as well. These are identifications of the specified maps, not choices of new adjunctions. No separatedness of the schemes over $k$ is needed.

source.place: Hom-bijection construction; domain checks and composition conventions

proof.text:
On a small pro-etale site $T$, the two cited ringed-site statements give, for ambient derived objects $U,V,B$, natural bijections
$$\operatorname{Hom}_T(U,H_T(V,B))\cong H^0(T,H_T(U,H_T(V,B)))\cong H^0(T,H_T(U\otimes_A^L V,B))\cong\operatorname{Hom}_T(U\otimes_A^L V,B).$$
They restrict to the full constructible categories by step 1. This derives the tensor–internal-Hom adjunction from the cited statements, rather than from preservation alone. Write $\operatorname{cur}$ and $\operatorname{unc}$ for the bijection and its inverse, so $\operatorname{unc}(v)=\mathrm{ev}\circ(v\otimes1)$. Naturality gives $\operatorname{unc}(b\circ v)=\operatorname{unc}(b)\circ(v\otimes1)$ whenever defined.

Record explicitly the meaning of the canonical exchange, including its direction. For $h:T\to S$, write $F_h\dashv G_h$, $L_h=Lh^*$, $B=H_T(L_hM,G_hN)$, and $\mathrm{ev}_h:B\otimes L_hM\to G_hN$. Write $\epsilon_h$ for the exceptional counit and $\operatorname{PF}_h$ for the projection map in the direction $F_hB\otimes M\to F_h(B\otimes L_hM)$. The canonical exchange $E_h:B\to G_hH_S(M,N)$ is the double transpose of
$$d_h=\epsilon_{h,N}\circ F_h(\mathrm{ev}_h)\circ\operatorname{PF}_{h,B,M}:F_hB\otimes M\to N.$$
Indeed, tensor–Hom transposition, exceptional transposition, precomposition by $\operatorname{PF}_h$, and the two reverse transpositions give exactly this map on $1_B$. This is the inverse of Varshavsky's (0.3): his (0.2) is the exceptional transpose of $\epsilon_h\otimes1$ after the inverse projection isomorphism; inserting it in his evaluation formula (0.3) reverses the displayed Hom bijections. In particular
$$\operatorname{unc}\bigl(\epsilon_{h,H_S(M,N)}\circ F_h(E_h)\bigr)=d_h.$$
This unpacks the specified canonical comparison, and does not infer coherence from the mere existence of an isomorphism. The projection theorem supplies invertibility and naturality on precisely these finite-Tor domains.

source.place: §0.3(a)-(b), equations (0.2)-(0.3); explicit inverse via the Hom bijections in the blueprint exchange proof

proof.text:
Let $\epsilon_c:FG\to1$, $\epsilon_j:fg\to1$, and write $e_C:H\otimes LM\to GN$ and $e_W:P\otimes lLM\to gGN$ for evaluation. Define
$$a=\epsilon_{j,H}\circ f(E_j):fP\to H.$$
The characterization in step 3, applied to $j$ with inputs $(LM,GN)$, says exactly
$$e_C\circ(a\otimes1)=\epsilon_{j,GN}\circ f(e_W)\circ\operatorname{PF}_{j,P,LM}.$$
All objects here were checked in step 1. This is an instance of the already established characterization, not a further compatibility assertion.

Transpose $r=g(E_c)\circ E_j:P\to gGQ$ under $Ff\dashv gG$. By the composite-adjunction counit its transpose is
$$\epsilon_{c,Q}\circ F(\epsilon_{j,GQ})\circ Ff(g(E_c))\circ Ff(E_j).$$
Naturality of $\epsilon_j$ at $E_c:H\to GQ$ rewrites this as $\epsilon_{c,Q}\circ F(E_c)\circ F(a)$. Uncurrying and step 3 for $c$, followed by naturality of $\operatorname{PF}_c$ at $a$, give
$$\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{unc}(\operatorname{adj}^{-1}(r))
&=\epsilon_{c,N}\circ F(e_C)\circ\operatorname{PF}_{c,H,M}\circ(F(a)\otimes1)\\
&=\epsilon_{c,N}\circ F(e_C\circ(a\otimes1))\circ\operatorname{PF}_{c,fP,M}\\
&=\epsilon_{c,N}\circ F(\epsilon_{j,GN})\circ Ff(e_W)\circ F(\operatorname{PF}_{j,P,LM})\circ\operatorname{PF}_{c,fP,M}.
\end{aligned}$$
The last equality substitutes step 4. Thus the right-hand side of the requested equality has been reduced to a specific arrow $FfP\otimes M\to N$.

source.place: Tag 0DV0, lemma-compose-counits; naturality of the projection transformation in the blueprint projection-formula theorem

proof.text:
Now transpose $s=\kappa_Q\circ E_{cj}$ under the same adjunction and uncurry. Because $\kappa$ is the conjugate of compact-support composition, the two transpositions for $cj$ are the composite transpositions after inserting $Ff\cong R(cj)_!$; this is precisely the Hom-bijection meaning of conjugation. Its counit is therefore $\epsilon_{c,N}\circ F(\epsilon_{j,GN})$, by the composite-adjunction formula. The composition compatibility in the projection-formula theorem states, under the pullback and compact-support composition comparisons,
$$\operatorname{PF}_{cj,P,M}=F(\operatorname{PF}_{j,P,LM})\circ\operatorname{PF}_{c,fP,M}.$$
To be explicit, the right-hand side has successive targets $F(fP\otimes LM)$ and $Ff(P\otimes lLM)$, the latter identified with $R(cj)_!(P\otimes L(cj)^*M)$. Evaluation $e_W$ is evaluation for this identified internal Hom; transport in its second variable uses $\kappa_N$, by naturality of tensor–Hom transposition. Consequently step 3 for $cj$ gives
$$\operatorname{unc}(\operatorname{adj}^{-1}(s))=\epsilon_{c,N}\circ F(\epsilon_{j,GN})\circ Ff(e_W)\circ F(\operatorname{PF}_{j,P,LM})\circ\operatorname{PF}_{c,fP,M}.$$
This is the same arrow as in step 5, with both the counit order and the projection-composition identifications specified.

source.place: Composition identity of the specified projection maps; Stacks Tag 0DV0 for the composite counit and Tag 0B65 for the conjugate comparison

proof.text: Exceptional adjunction and tensor–Hom transposition are bijections on these Hom sets. Steps 5 and 6 have identical images under their composite, so $s=r$. Restoring the notation gives $\kappa_Q\circ E_{cj}=Rj^!(E_c)\circ E_j$, with the source comparison using $\kappa_N$ and $L(cj)^*\cong Lj^*Lc^*$. We never interchange tensor factors: evaluation throughout is $H(-,-)\otimes(\text{first input})\to(\text{second input})$. Thus the result is the stated equality of canonical maps, without an extra permutation or sign.
